title: Ordinary semilinear system calculus and cartesian internal Hom
statement: For an essentially small site C with independent site and coefficient universes and any inverse sequence B of commutative ring sheaves, the ordinary derived category of modules on the ringed sequence site has a Data structure as in [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus], together with its HomReductionFormula. This includes Grothendieck abelianness, componentwise exactness, exact and jointly conservative derived evaluation, normalized scalar adjunctions and their reduction cocycle, representative-normalized tensor and cartesian-input internal Hom, and the displayed Hom transition law. No geometric morphism, open localization or compatible second ring tower is part of this result.

proof.text: Present the sequence topos by the small site $\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\geq1}$: an arrow $(U,n)\to(W,m)$ consists of $U\to W$ and $n\leq m$, and generating covers have fixed index and are covers of $\mathcal C$. Pulling back such a cover along an index-changing arrow still gives a fixed-index cover, so this is a site. Its sheaf condition says exactly that each level is a sheaf; the other restrictions give inverse-sequence transitions. The ring sheaf $(U,n)\mapsto B_n(U)$ is therefore $B_\bullet$, and its module sheaves are exactly $\mathscr S(B)$. Kernels and cokernels are computed at each level using kernels and sheafified cokernels of module sheaves; the scalar-linear transitions descend to these constructions. Hence cohomology of a complex of systems is componentwise.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to that small ringed site. This gives Grothendieck abelianness and unbounded K-injective resolutions in $\mathscr S(B)$. Exact evaluation descends termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. A morphism in the derived category is invertible exactly when its cone is acyclic; its evaluated cones are the cones of its evaluations. Componentwise cohomology therefore proves joint detection of isomorphisms. This uses only localization of complexes of systems, not a category of diagrams in triangulated categories.

proof.text: On underlying sequence topoi, evaluation $e_n$ is inverse image of a geometric morphism: its right adjoint sends a sheaf $F$ to the sequence with value $F$ for $q\geq n$ and terminal sheaf for $q<n$. The adjunction follows by extending the component at $n$ along the given transitions; evaluation preserves finite limits. The structural ring map is $e_nB_\bullet=B_n$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] says evaluation carries flat-term K-flat complexes on the sequence site to flat-term K-flat complexes over $B_n$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on that site and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]: evaluating the resulting total tensor complexes computes $e_n(M\otimes^L_{B_\bullet}N)=M_n\otimes^L_{B_n}N_n$. The comparisons on morphisms are induced by actual tensor chain maps and inversion of quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: For a $B_n$-module $F$, define $(E_nF)_q=F\otimes_{B_n}B_q$ for $q\leq n$ and zero for $q>n$, with quotient-induced transitions. A map $h:F\to M_n$ extends uniquely to $E_nF\to M$: its component at $q\leq n$ is $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,\tau_{nq}(h(x))$, and above $n$ the source is zero. Balancing and the transition cocycle verify this formula; evaluating at $n$ recovers $h$. This proves the natural adjunction $E_n\dashv e_n$ by the module tensor/restriction adjunction. These formulas also commute with the Hom-complex differential $d(h)=d_Mh-(-1)^{|h|}hd_F$, giving the adjunction on homotopy categories.

proof.text: The additive functor $QE_n$ preserves shifts and cone matrices. Every complex over $B_n$ has a flat-term K-flat resolution [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. A quasi-isomorphism between such complexes remains a quasi-isomorphism after each tensor $-\otimes_{B_n}B_q$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1), and hence after $E_n$ by componentwise cohomology. The resolving-class criterion [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] gives an everywhere-defined $L_n=LE_n$, computed by $E_nP$ on those representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], exact evaluation is its own everywhere-defined right derived functor, so [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] gives $L_n\dashv e_n$. In particular $e_qL_nP=P\otimes^L_{B_n}B_q$ for $q\leq n$ and is zero otherwise. No coefficient-flatness hypothesis entered this argument.

proof.text: For $m\geq n$, put $T_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$. There is a natural map $\sigma_{mn}:L_nT_{m,n}\to L_m$: on a flat-term K-flat $P$ over $B_m$, its components are the tensor rebracketing identity $P\otimes_{B_m}B_q$ for $q\leq n$ and the zero-source map for $q>n$. K-flat pullback ensures the iterated tensors compute the displayed functors. Resolving-class tensor descent makes this a transformation of functors on the derived categories. Both composites for three indices have precisely the same components as chain maps on the same representative, so they are equal after localization. The derived adjunction sends precomposition with $\sigma_{mn}$ to $h\mapsto t_{m,n}T_{m,n}(h)$: this is the tensor-adjoint formula $x\otimes a\mapsto a\tau_{mn}h(x)$. It follows that the $t_{m,n}$ are natural and satisfy their cocycle. Invertibility of adjacent reductions implies invertibility of all reductions by this cocycle and preservation of isomorphisms by tensor; this proves the stated normalization criterion.

proof.text:
On any of the small ringed sites in use, define $H(M,N)$ by the K-injective construction [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; its independence is [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]. The internal-Hom identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and the global-sections identification of [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,H(M,N))\cong H^0R\Gamma H(P,H(M,N))\cong H^0R\Gamma H(P\otimes^LM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes^LM,N).$$
These bijections are natural. Hence they define the tensor-Hom adjunction and its evaluation on the sequence site as well as on each level. This supplies the system internal Hom without trying to assemble unrelated fiber objects.

proof.text:
Let $M$ be cartesian. There is a canonical system map
$$L_n(P\otimes^L_{B_n}M_n)\cong L_nP\otimes^L_{B_\bullet}L_nM_n\longrightarrow L_nP\otimes^L_{B_\bullet}M,$$
where the last arrow uses the counit $L_ne_nM\to M$. For the first isomorphism take flat-term K-flat representatives over $B_n$. Their $E_n$ extensions are K-flat with flat terms: below $n$ this is K-flat pullback, above $n$ zero; componentwise exactness and tensor then test K-flatness of these particular systems. The ordinary tensor rebracketing gives the isomorphism on these strict models and descends by tensor descent. At $q\leq n$ the second arrow is $T_{n,q}P\otimes^L t^M_{n,q}$, which is invertible by cartesianness, and above $n$ it is $0\to0$. Joint detection therefore makes the displayed projection map an isomorphism of derived systems. This is a constructed map, not an inference of equality from evaluations.

proof.text:
For every $P\in D(B_n)$, apply the adjunctions and the preceding projection isomorphism to obtain
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_nH_B(M,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_nP,H_B(M,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_nP\otimes^LM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_n(P\otimes^LM_n),N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes^LM_n,N_n)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,H_{B_n}(M_n,N_n)).$$
Yoneda gives the claimed natural internal-Hom comparison. Its definition by these transposes carries system evaluation to the fiber evaluation. Transpose the reduction transition of the system evaluation map. Since $t^M_{m,n}$ is invertible, the resulting equation uniquely determines the reduction of $H_B(M,N)$: it is exactly the transpose of the formula displayed in the statement. The cocycle holds as an equation of system maps because evaluation and its adjunction were constructed on the sequence site; alternatively its two transposes are the same twice-reassociated evaluation followed by the transition of $N$, by the tensor associators. The inverse cartesian comparison is essential here.
